utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-65-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Mejakic, Momcilo Gruban, Dusan Fustar, and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May we have the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Joanna Korner, Ann Sutherland and Michael McVicker assisted by Ruth Karper, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Jovan Simic attorney-at-law representing Mr. Zeljko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you try again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am attorney-at-law Jovan Simic representing Zeljko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. Milenko Dundjer attorney-at-law representing Mr. Gruban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Theodore Scudder representing the defendant Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Slobodanka Nedic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade representing Mr. Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We begin this Status Conference first by looking at the pending motions of which there are five. I'll just set them out, and say what the status is in relation to each. There is a Prosecution 92 bis motion. We expect that this will be dealt with in due course. It does require some attention because of the length. There are ten binders, but we expect to deal with it, as I said, in due course. Then there is a motion for judicial notice, and we expect that will be dealt with within the next week or two. There is also a second motion relating to conflict of interest, and that will be dealt with also within that time frame. For the next two motions, I'd like us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Pre-trial briefs, all the pre-trial briefs are now ready. The revised consolidated pre-trial brief from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Prosecution was accepted by the Trial Chamber, and the Knezevic Defence team filed a supplementary brief in response, and the Mejakic Defence also filed a pre-trial brief. So all these submissions are now complete, and that is good. Disclosure. All disclosure, I understand, in relation to 66(A)(i) and (ii) have been made with the exception of one translation of a witness statement, number 17, and I believe that that has now been done. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. It had already been disclosed, but it hadn't reached Mr. Scudder. So it's been redisclosed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. There is an issue relating to the photo boards used for identification, but that is not a disclosure matter, and that's a matter that will be settled otherwise. I'm taking it, then, that all disclosure has been made, and I make this point because I understand that on certain occasions some of the Defence team have said that they have not received all the -- all the items. It is, of course, the duty of the Defence to check items which are submitted to them on the basis of disclosure to ensure that they have received what they should receive, and I'm taking it, unless I hear to the contrary, that disclosure in terms of 66(A)(i) and (ii) is complete. As regards Rule 68 disclosure, the Prosecution has completed its review, and disclosure of material in the Kvocka appeal, I think that is -- that's an ongoing obligation in any event. With regard to 68 material arising from interviews with Predrag Banovic, I understand that there is an issue there as to whether something more than the extracts should be disclosed. I don't know whether any of the Defence counsel would like to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've disclosed the Rule 68 from that interview. There's been a request from Mr. Scudder on behalf of Fustar for the whole interview, and at the moment we've complied as was stated yesterday in the Rule 65 ter conference. We have complied with our obligation to disclose the Rule 68. The question of the rest of the interview with Mr. Banovic is something that we're still in the process of considering as to whether or not we need to disclose the whole interview, and that would only arise if and when he is a Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. As far as witnesses are concerned, Ms. Korner, you're still at 57, 57 witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And on the basis of that, the examination-in-chief would take something in the region of six weeks plus time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, we've estimated six weeks for the Prosecution case, depending on the length of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So that the case could be completed within six months.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It should be able to, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, this case is really now ready for trial, and it is the expectation that it will come on for trial sometime in the autumn depending on the availability of Trial Chambers. So that I would like to fix a date for the next Status Conference or Pre-Trial Conference, depending on whether trial can take place, and that date would be Wednesday, the 7th of July for either a Status Conference or a Pre-Trial Conference. Let us hope it will be a Pre-Trial Conference. May I now ask whether any of the Defence counsel have anything to say before I turn to the accused themselves. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Mejakic has no new issues to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me turn to the accused themselves to ascertain from them whether they have anything to say in respect of their conditions of detention or indeed any other matter relating to the trial. First the accused Mejakic. Mr. Mejakic, please stand. THE ACCUSED MEJAKIC: [Interpretation] I have no questions or comments, Your Honour. I feel fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The accused Dusan Fustar. Mr. Fustar, please stand. THE ACCUSED FUSTAR: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaints. I feel fine in the Detention Unit. The guards are treating us well and everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Fustar. And Dusko Knezevic. Mr. Knezevic, please stand. THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] I have nothing to say, Your Honour. I am in good health, and I would like to say everything -- I would like to say that the Detention Unit and the administration of the prison are very good to us indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, full marks for the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just mention one matter about the estimate of six weeks, and that's this: It is, of course, very much dependent on the agreed facts issue, because obviously if we have to -- it was explained yesterday in the 65 ter conference if there is still a continued dispute about the background, we will have to call an additional witness to deal with the background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it is dependent on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We take that into account, Ms. Korner. Thank you. If there is no other matter, the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
